rule: Review КТ5: every provision whose draft open point is implementation_only is read against the pinned text before it is counted as resolvable or covered. 'confirmed': the text fixes what is required and no author choice is needed; the lab adds a check. 'reclassified': an author decision or a missing definition blocks it; origin_after names it. A checkable correction is recorded with the decision.
closure_rule: Review of checkpoint 6: for each confirmed provision the draft open point (implementation_only) is closed once the missing lab check exists, unless something else remains. 'closed': the agent's reading answers the draft need from the text (answer); decision_status becomes NONE_IDENTIFIED by agent reading, the open point is removed, and the draft classification and reason stay in this record. 'open': a missing formula, an undefined criterion, an external artifact or a contested reading remains; the open point stays with that origin and reason. A partial check (coverage PARTIAL) is a limit of coverage, not an open point. Nothing here is a human acceptance (A6).
reading_rule: Review of checkpoint 6: the remaining open points of uncovered provisions, whose origin was a Codex draft, are read one by one against the pinned corpus (all 38 documents), as the implementation_only drafts were. 'kept': the draft origin holds; the open point stays, now as the lab's reading; partial_check says whether a clear core could be checked without deciding the open point. 'reclassified': another origin blocks it (origin_after). 'returned': the corpus settles what the draft said was missing (most often a reference to a corpus document read as external); the provision is resolvable (implementation_only) and needs a lab check; once the check exists it carries a closure like a confirmed decision. Nothing here is a human acceptance (A6).
core_revision_rule: Review КТ7-GPT-01: a provision marked partial_check: true is unfinished work while it is uncovered. Each such clear part is checked, or, when the check cannot confirm it (the part would be checked only as a label, needs the open point itself, or needs a change to the published bench), the flag is set to false with an individual reason; the earlier value and the reason stay in partial_check_revised. No flag is dropped to regain a stage status.
covered_reading_rule: Review of checkpoint 7, step 4: the 208 provisions that were covered (IMPLEMENTED or PARTIAL) while their open point was still the Codex draft label implementation_only are read one by one with the scheme of the closure_rule. A check of the whole provision or of a part does not by itself remove the open point: each reading states whether the text answers the draft need (closed, with the answer) or what remains (open, with origin and reason). A PARTIAL coverage is a limit of coverage, not an open point. Nothing here is a human acceptance (A6).

AISUBJECT-1-03.reason: Learned preferences and emergent strategies need behavioural evidence. Core: for a declared conflict between a goal and a constraint, the constraint prevails.

AISUBJECT-1-04.reason: 'Decide direction' versus 'execute or stop' is drawn by §2 of the same text: the AI enumerates admissible actions without ranking, the authorizing Subject chooses, and a declared deterministic rule is execution.

closure.answer: §2.2-§2.3 fix it: choosing among admissible actions is the Subjects'; a deterministic rule or a halt is execution. A selection by the agent's preference is the observable breach.

AISUBJECT-2-02.reason: Enumeration within constraints and simulation of consequences are permitted; ranking is not. Feasibility is the constraint set the agent receives; an order or score that compares options is ranking.

closure.answer: Feasible = admissible under the given constraints (the input set). Any comparative order or score is ranking; options passed through in input order are not ranked.

AISUBJECT-2-05.reason: Concretized by §8.3 (halt upon conflict): on a declared value conflict the AI halts and escalates; an output that resolves it is observable.

closure.answer: Concretized by §8.3 (halt upon conflict): a resolution by the agent is observable.

AISUBJECT-2-06.reason: The provision forbids replacing human choice by the agent's preference. With §1.4 and §2 the replacement is a selection made by the agent without a deterministic rule.

closure.answer: Plurality of human decision is kept when selection stays with Subjects or a declared rule; an agent selection by preference is the replacement the text forbids.

AISUBJECT-3-01.reason: Responsibility maps to the authorizing Subject or deploying entity; IDENTITY §5-§6 give the mapping of proxies to their originating Subject.

closure.answer: The authorizing Subject is named in each agent record; IDENTITY §5 supplies the originator for deployed mechanisms. 'The model decided' is the observable breach.

AISUBJECT-5-01.reason: PTL data are authoritative: the agent relays them unchanged and halts on crossings (§5); conflicts between readings are ORACLE's (§11 divergence), not the agent's.

closure.answer: Authoritative = relayed without smoothing, suppression or override (AI-SUBJECT §5); conflicting readings are represented and arbitrated by ORACLE §11.

AISUBJECT-7-04.reason: Whose authority and how compared is open.

AISUBJECT-7-06.reason: Durations are not given. Core: each crisis action has a declared end.

AISUBJECT-7-07.reason: AUDIT is in the corpus and defines audit mechanisms (§6: signed execution traces, state hashing, independent recomputation) and covers crisis invocations (§4). Each crisis action has a trace and recomputes from recorded inputs.

closure.answer: AUDIT is in the corpus (§6 mechanisms; §4 covers crisis invocations).

AISUBJECT-7-08.reason: Precedent is concretized in the corpus (CRISIS-0-03, CRISIS-Non-PrecedentRule_-03, WORKCYCLE-10-05 closed): a later rule or decision citing a crisis action as authority is observable.

closure.answer: Precedent is concretized in the corpus (CRISIS-0-03 and others): a rule drawn from the crisis action.

AISUBJECT-7-09.reason: CRISIS and the Code are in the corpus, so not external; 'narrowly authorized oracle TTL extensions' meets ORACLE §14 ('DOES NOT modify TTL values'), the conflict of Q-027. Core: no TTL extension without an explicit Crisis/Mercy authorization record.

AISUBJECT-8-02.reason: Implicit authority from learning needs a capability model. Core: the permitted action set after learning is within the set before.

ANTITERROR-0-01.reason: 'Deliberate targeting' and 'intent' stand against §2's ban on inferring intent; the tension is real.

ANTITERROR-0-02.reason: 'Strictly defensive and containment-oriented' is concretized by §6 (permitted containment actions) and §8 (termination on cessation): every anti-terror action is a §6 containment measure taken while a confirmed stream lasts; offensive, punitive or retaliatory actions are observable.

closure.answer: The classification is given by the text: containment = the §6 permitted actions while a confirmed stream lasts (§8 termination).

ANTITERROR-1-01.reason: JUSTICE is in the corpus. An ANTITERROR record that imposes a Justice outcome or a sanction is observable (§4.3 excludes punishment).

closure.answer: JUSTICE is in the corpus; a sanction or an override of a Justice decision by ANTITERROR is a recorded act (§4.3, §11).

ANTITERROR-10-01.reason: ORACLE, TIME and JUSTICE are in the corpus: each record carries a DTI-Day index and a PTL anchor and is open to post-event and Justice review. Metadata presence and access are observable.

closure.answer: ORACLE, TIME and JUSTICE are in the corpus; DTI index, log and forwarding for review are recorded properties.

ANTITERROR-11-01.reason: ANTITERROR modifies no economic protocol and imposes no sanction; downstream triggering via other protocols is separate from an ANTITERROR-executed sanction.

closure.answer: An economic or sanction act whose executor is ANTITERROR is the breach; RED isolation via downstream protocols (§9) is not.

ANTITERROR-11-02.reason: Two isolation bans: no regulation of speech or ideology (observable as content filtering), no override of Defense or Justice decisions (observable as a recorded override).

closure.answer: §6.3 itself separates technical information isolation (signal amplitude) from content control; overrides are recorded acts.

ANTITERROR-2-01.reason: Execution order and the coordination interface are not defined.

ANTITERROR-2-02.reason: No inference of ideology, intent, belief or affiliation and no collective responsibility; both are observable as inferred fields or measures on associates.

closure.answer: Inferred-trait fields and measures on associates of the attacker are the excluded acts.

ANTITERROR-3.1-01.reason: 'High destabilization relative to physical scale' needs a threshold.

ANTITERROR-3.1-02.reason: IMPACT is in the corpus, so not external; 'sharp', 'abrupt' and 'overload' need cut-offs.

ANTITERROR-4.2-01.reason: No profiling by belief, religion, ethnicity or politics, no intent from speech or association, identity not a risk signal; observable as measures on people selected by these features.

closure.answer: Selection by a protected feature or by association is the breach; observed as detention of associates (coverage limit).

ANTITERROR-4.3-01.reason: 'Immediate recurrence' needs a horizon. Core: each action cites one of the three objectives and falls within a confirmed stream (as ANTITERROR-0-02).

ANTITERROR-4.3-02.reason: Concretized as ANTITERROR-0-02 was closed: punitive, deterrent or retaliatory action shows as action outside the §6 containment list or after the stream ends (§8).

closure.answer: Concretized as ANTITERROR-0-02: punitive or retaliatory action shows as action outside §6 or after the stream ends (§8).

closure.answer: T1 entry and its permission are fixed by the text; 'localized' is relative to the confirmed stream's zone. 'Immediate' is a permission, not a deadline.

ANTITERROR-5-03.reason: The counting window and the coordination interface are not given.

ANTITERROR-8-01.reason: 'Rapid' needs a time. Core: ANTITERROR records no infrastructure shielding (the role of DEFENSE).

ANTITERROR-8-03.reason: Post-factum to the action or to the event is open. Core: Justice records cite PTL evidence and follow the action.

ANTITERROR-9-02.reason: Whether non-viability is a required result or an intended effect is open; RED mechanisms are downstream.

closure.answer: JUSTICE and ORACLE are in the corpus; §4 (bases) and §5 (persistence) make the definition concrete.

ASSETS-1-02.reason: 'Externalize harm' needs a system boundary that ASSETS does not define (§6 repeats 'beyond system boundaries'). Core: an asset action that exceeds a declared axiom bound, or changes an IMPACT or JUSTICE output, is a violation.

ASSETS-10-01.reason: Transfer needs explicit transfer of obligations, acceptance of ongoing responsibility, and compliance with current impact constraints by the asset's use at the moment of transfer.

closure.answer: Compliance is that of the transferred asset's current use, assessed at transfer for the receiving Subject; the three conditions are observable.

ASSETS-11-01.reason: Control over non-essential assets is restricted or suspended under §11; 'non-essential' has no criterion, and the relation to §8.1 revocation is not stated.

closure.reason: Asset essentiality has no criterion; declared per asset.

ASSETS-11-03.reason: ASSETS applies the Justice outcome as given: no waiver of a Restriction, Isolation or Exclusion and no non-essential control kept under it. Observable on ASSETS records.

closure.answer: Overriding a Justice outcome = ASSETS changing or waiving it; §11 states the effects ASSETS applies.

ASSETS-12-01.reason: IDENTITY is in the corpus. The list is plain: every ownership or control structure is registered, publicly auditable (its record is readable), and bound to identified Subjects. Each property is observable on the asset register.

closure.answer: IDENTITY is in the corpus; registration, public auditability and binding to a Subject are properties of the register.

ASSETS-13-01.reason: JUSTICE, IMPACT and AXIOMS are in the corpus. Four bans with a clear core, as FINANCE-1-01 and JUSTICE-13-01: an ASSETS record that changes a Justice outcome, writes an impact measurement, applies a discretionary rule or grants an axiom exemption is observable.

closure.answer: JUSTICE, IMPACT and AXIOMS are in the corpus; a waiver, override or discretionary grant by ASSETS is a recorded act.

ASSETS-2-01.reason: 'Above', 'alongside' and 'below' have no defined relation. Core: data flow from PTL into ASSETS, never the reverse.

ASSETS-3.1-01.reason: Classifying real entities by controllability, measurable impact and enabled functions needs evidence.

ASSETS-3.2-01.reason: The definition fixes observable properties of every right: granted by system rule, conditional (persistence conditions, §5), revocable, not permanent; when a condition fails the right is degraded (§5 'No Property Right is permanent').

closure.answer: §5 lists the persistence conditions and the consequence of their failure (degradation, restriction, suspension).

ASSETS-4-01.reason: Projections and capacity sufficiency need models; 'non-negative' is explicit. Core: a grant only with all four declared conditions true.

ASSETS-4-02.reason: Three excluded bases; a request resting on prior possession, inheritance without obligation transfer or a contract detached from impact alone is refused. Observable with the basis declared.

closure.answer: The three excluded bases are named; 'solely' makes the test the absence of any §4 a-d basis.

ASSETS-5-01.reason: 'Restitution obligations are satisfied' may mean complete discharge or current installments. Core: the non-negative Justice condition.

ASSETS-5-02.reason: The response set is closed (degradation, restriction or suspension, any of them) and automatic; the property_rights module already requires one of the three on or before every failure day (ASSETS-3.2-01, review КТ6-GPT-02). closure.answer: The response set is closed and automatic; what degradation does beyond being one of the three is not needed for the rule.

ASSETS-6-01.reason: The system boundary is not defined. Core: use of an asset to bypass attribution (a transfer that removes the responsible Subject) is observable.

ASSETS-6-02.reason: A permission ('constitutes grounds'); the increase in risk or damage needs a baseline and attribution.

ASSETS-7-01.reason: The responses are clear (graduated restrictions, enforced divestment, reallocation), but the trigger is not decidable: 'Concentration thresholds are derived from impact metrics' gives no values. ASSETS-7-02.reason: The threshold derivation is missing; the basis is fixed. Core (as H-FM-3): thresholds unchanged when only valuation or market price changes.

ASSETS-8.2-02.reason: How the three priorities compare is not given.

ASSETS-8.3-05.reason: Filing a revocation dispute is no ground for restrictions; reliance on the filing is observable as a measure derived from the dispute record.

closure.answer: A measure whose provenance includes the dispute filing is the prohibited prejudice.

ASSETS-9-01.reason: The listed categories are designated Non-Privatizable or Conditionally Privatizable and, per the next sentence, held only under stewardship and always revocable. Which category is which is not assigned by the text (declared, H-PR-1), but the provision holds for either: designation recorded, never ordinary private property.

closure.reason: The text does not assign each listed category to Non-Privatizable or Conditionally Privatizable and gives no membership criterion ('biosphere-critical', 'essential commons'); declared per category (H-PR-1).

ASSETS-9-02.reason: 'Strict stewardship conditions' is undefined rather than open to two readings. Core: such assets always remain revocable (a record making one irrevocable is a violation).

ASSETS-ReallocationTransparencyConstrain.reason: Reallocation must be auditable, traceable to justice outcomes and impact constraints, and deterministic; rule and provenance are recorded and replayed.

closure.answer: Traceability = provenance to the Justice and impact records; determinism = identical replay. Public observability is a coverage limit.

ASSETS-ReallocationTransparencyConstrain.reason: No discretionary authority, closed committee or opaque body may control reallocation; observable as a reallocation decided by a body instead of the rule.

closure.answer: A reallocation record whose decider is not the published rule is the prohibited control.

ASSETS-ReallocationTransparencyConstrain.reason: 'Algorithmic custodianship under open rules, not bureaucratic management': the custodian of an asset under public stewardship is an algorithmic custodian bound to the open rule, not an administrative body. Observable on the reallocation record.

closure.answer: The two preceding sentences of the constraint fix the criterion: deterministic rule-based procedure, no discretionary body.

AUDIT-1-01.reason: 'Permanent structural condition' means no operating interval without audit. Over a discrete stream that is an audit record for every event; the module checks it on the declared stream (a coverage limit).

closure.answer: Permanent = no operating event without its audit record; continuity is checked event by event. The declared stream limits coverage, not the meaning.

AUDIT-1-02.reason: Audit verifies execution and does not judge outcomes; §8 lists its responses as procedural and §10 limits it to observing and reporting.

closure.answer: AUDIT §8 and §10 classify the outputs: procedural notices and reports are verification; a sanction or an outcome judgement is what the text excludes.

AUDIT-10-01.reason: Observe and report only: a change to live execution sourced from audit is the observable breach; escalation is a report to another layer (§8), not an act of audit.

closure.answer: Audit-caused changes are records whose source is audit and which alter execution; reports and escalations change nothing themselves.

AUDIT-11-02.reason: Mercy may change response severity, not audit visibility: visibility is the continuity of audit logging during Mercy, which is observable.

closure.answer: Visibility = uninterrupted audit logging; the sentence permits severity changes and forbids visibility changes, so only the latter is checked.

AUDIT-12-02.reason: 'Any modification requires a new protocol identifier', and the same section states that presentation-only corrections are not Upgrades and are recorded by the 'Last updated' date.

closure.answer: §12 answers it: presentation-only corrections that do not change normative content are not modifications under the procedure; every normative change needs a new identifier.

AUDIT-12-04.reason: The compatibility declaration with SCOPE belongs to the change procedure; §12 itself takes presentation-only corrections out of that procedure.

closure.answer: §12: presentation-only corrections are not Upgrades, so they need no compatibility declaration; every normative modification does.

AUDIT-2-01.reason: SCOPE is in the corpus; the layer relations remain undefined.

AUDIT-2-02.reason: Audit outputs shall not override or substitute decisions; an audit output that alters or replaces a decision is observable as an audit-sourced act on it.

closure.answer: Effects are attributed by provenance: an audit record that supersedes or changes a decision is the prohibited act. The module observes live modifications (coverage limit).

AUDIT-3-03.reason: An Audit Invariant must hold 'at all times'; in a discrete, DTI-indexed log the relevant times are the recorded events and steps.

closure.answer: All times = every recorded event and step of the log; the invariant is evaluated at each.

AUDIT-4-01.reason: The provision lists the activity types under continuous audit; coverage is an audit record for every activity of those types.

closure.answer: The list fixes the types; continuous = every activity of a listed type has its audit record.

AUDIT-5-01.reason: The listed invariants must be verified continuously, i.e. at every recorded event.

closure.answer: Continuous verification = each listed invariant evaluated at every recorded event of the stream.

AUDIT-5.3-02.reason: Runtime tuning, adaptive optimization and silent calibration are one act seen three ways: a parameter change during execution outside the declared change procedure.

closure.answer: Observable as a parameter change in the log that did not pass UPGRADE; 'silent' is the absence of that declared change.

AUDIT-6-01.reason: The four means (signature and hash verification, replay, independent recomputation, consistency checks) are named, but no signature scheme or replica environment is.

closure.reason: The signature scheme and the independent recomputation environment are not specified; the lab uses SHA-256 digests and a declared replica result.

AUDIT-8-05.reason: Audit applies no punishment; §8 lists the procedural responses, so any sanction or penalty is outside them.

closure.answer: §8's list of responses is the classification: anything that sanctions or penalizes is punitive.

AUDIT-9-01.reason: Results must be accessible for independent verification and expose the methodology; neither 'independent' nor sufficient access is defined.

closure.reason: Who counts as an independent verifier and what access suffices are not defined; checked as recorded properties.

AUDIT-9-02.reason: Proprietary, closed and authority-gated are properties of an audit process: its licence, its access and the permission it requires.

closure.answer: Each prohibited restriction is a property of the process record (licence, access, gate); checked on recorded properties (coverage limit).

AXIOMS-1-01.reason: No higher-layer protocol may violate an axiom regardless of benefit; whether a given act violates an axiom needs the measurement of each axiom (A1's minimum required conditions are undefined, F-023).

closure.reason: Mapping an act to an axiom violation needs the impact and survival models of the axioms; violations are declared per candidate.

AXIOMS-2-01.reason: Genesis Block #0 is not in the corpus (cf. CODEX-Glossary_Definitions-06). Core: the layer order is checkable as data flow (AXIOMS reads PTL outputs; impact, justice and economic stages consume AXIOMS outputs, never the reverse).

AXIOMS-2-02.reason: The Equation is in the corpus (Code, Appendix A.1: dW/dt >= k·E·T·B^2.83, A.1a governance), so it is not external; what 'compatible' requires of an interpretation is not defined. Core: no AXIOMS output changes Equation parameters (A.1a).

AXIOMS-2-03.reason: 'Axioms do not process data; they constrain how data-derived metrics may be interpreted and acted upon': the axiom stage records which axioms a candidate violates and the constrained choice, and computes no metric of its own. Observable on the axiom stage's records.

closure.answer: Axioms constrain; they compute no metric. The axiom stage's records show which kind of output it produces.

AXIOMS-3-01.reason: Each axiom is either a forbidden state or a hard priority ordering; the wording of A1-A7 places each in one form (A1, A2, A5, A6 forbid; A3, A4, A7 order; lab reading H-AX-5), and none may be encoded as a weighted term (§3, §7). Observable on the recorded forms and the decision basis.

closure.answer: The verdict depends only on each axiom being one of the two forms and none being a weighted term; the assignment of an axiom to a form (H-AX-5, a model hypothesis) does not change it.

AXIOMS-7-05.reason: Reinterpreting an axiom by context is observable as a recorded violation excused by political, cultural or situational context; changes of meaning go through §8 modification.

closure.answer: A contextual excuse of a violation is the reinterpretation the text names; a meaning change is a §8 modification with a new identifier.

AXIOMS-8-01.reason: Axioms are invariant once deployed, and §8 makes any change a new protocol with a new identifier, incompatibility declaration and simulation.

closure.answer: Invariance is identity of the deployed text: §8 routes every change through a new identifier.

AXIOMS-AxiomA2-SystemicSustainability-02.reason: The persistence duration and the degradation baseline are parameters. Core: under a declared window, an action with sustained B(t) degradation is flagged.

AXIOMS-AxiomA3-PhysicalRealitySupremacy-.reason: Decisions must be grounded in PTL outputs; grounding is a provenance relation to PTL outputs (EB §5 metadata, AUDIT traceability).

closure.answer: Grounding = provenance from PTL outputs; the module takes it as declared (coverage limit).

AXIOMS-AxiomA3-PhysicalRealitySupremacy-.reason: A candidate resting on a declared goal, narrative or belief that contradicts the PTL measurement violates A3 and cannot prevail over an axiom-clean candidate. Observable with the basis and the contradiction declared per candidate.

closure.answer: A3's first sentence fixes the representation: decisions grounded in PTL outputs; a narrative against PTL cannot prevail.

AXIOMS-AxiomA5-ExternalityAccountability.reason: Whether a documented bound suffices or an admissibility limit is needed is open. Core: an action that shifts harm across the boundary without any measurement of the externality is a violation.

AXIOMS-AxiomA7-MinimumSufferingConstrain.reason: The proxy mapping from S(t) to suffering needs data. Core: suffering never appears as an objective or optimization target.

AXIOMS-EpistemicClarification-04.reason: 'Bounded evaluation constraints, not metaphysical assertions': the axioms are published as constraints with no claim of absolute truth (their application outputs are disputable: EpistemicClarification-02/03). Observable on the published definitions.

CODEX-15.1-01.reason: Algorithms influencing resource allocation, social rating or news feeds must be open source; which algorithms 'influence' these domains needs a tracing rule the Code does not give.

closure.reason: Influence on the three domains has no tracing rule; the domains of each algorithm are declared.

CODEX-2-01.reason: 'First independent jurisdiction or city-state' narrows A.5's 'any entity'; who may take the Alpha slot and what 'fully implement' and 'without prior agreements' require is a contested reading (cf. the Wild Node residual on CODEX-Glossary_Definitions-05). Core: the slot stays empty until a qualifying node is declared.

CODEX-2.1-01.reason: Global-fund financing only through targeted smart contracts; neither a registry of global funds nor a criterion for 'targeted' is given.

closure.reason: Global funds and qualifying targets have no registry or criterion; channel and target are declared.

CODEX-3-01.reason: The explanatory note restates that the message is embedded in block #0 and unchangeable; checkable as presence and immutability of the specified message over the run. 'Forever' is beyond any run, and the characterization of the message is not judged (partial).

closure.answer: Presence and immutability of the specified message; the note's characterization of it is descriptive, not a rule.

CODEX-6.1-01.reason: An absolute right to leave admits no condition; any delay, fee or condition attached to leaving is a restriction (as EXIT §0 and §10 state in the corpus).

closure.answer: Absolute = unconditional; delays, fees and conditions on exit are the restrictions, observable on exit records.

CODEX-9.1-01.reason: Irremovable power is abolished and territories are run by Regional Operators; no test of removability is given.

closure.reason: Irremovability has no criterion (term, recall procedure); it is a declared flag.

CODEX-9.2-01.reason: Operators are hired per KPI and terminated automatically on failure; the KPI deadline and failure condition are terms of each contract, not of the Code.

closure.answer: Deadlines and failure conditions are contract inputs; the Code's rule is automatic termination on failure, which is observable.

CODEX-A.1a-01.reason: Equation coefficients and bounds are not tuned on-chain or in execution; A.1a gives the only channel, UPGRADE with prior simulation.

closure.answer: Any parameter change outside UPGRADE (on-chain or during execution) is the prohibited tuning.

CODEX-A.1a-03.reason: No operational, financial, crisis or enforcement protocol may modify Equation parameters directly or indirectly; the categories are protocol layers and every change must come through UPGRADE.

CODEX-Glossary_Definitions-04.reason: 'Ecocide' is not defined anywhere in the corpus (missing definition rather than data), and the choice between burning and redistribution is not fixed beyond Article 7 for aggression. Core: on a confirmed violation the stake is burned or redistributed automatically, never returned; for aggression it is burned.

CODEX-Glossary_Definitions-05.reason: The definition fixes three properties of a Wild Node: independent party, no prior coordination with the founders, full protocol compliance. With coordination and compliance as declared node properties, admission on compliance alone is observable.

closure.reason: 'Prior coordination with the founders' and 'independent party' have no criterion; whether a node is a Wild Node (and so whether A.5 launch conditions hold) rests on a declared property.

CODEX-Glossary_Definitions-06.reason: 'Cryptographically embedded ... impossible to delete or edit': the message is part of the content hashed into block #0, so any edit changes the digest; edit and delete requests are refused. The Code gives no block hash, so the digest is the lab's (partial).

closure.reason: The real Genesis Block #0 and its hash are not in the corpus; embedding is checked only on a lab digest of the specified block.

CODEX-Preamble-01.reason: The three forms in which power is held are concretized elsewhere in the Code: algorithms are immutable except by UPGRADE with simulation (A.1a), metrics are public (PTL readings of B(t)), liability is automated (A.3, A.6, §7.3, §8). Each is an observable property of execution; the fourth item (incentives) is a separate provision.

closure.answer: The Code itself makes the three forms concrete: immutability except by UPGRADE with simulation (A.1a), public PTL metrics (A.2), automated liability (A.3, A.6, §7.3, §8).

CODEX-Preamble-02.reason: Algorithms 'do not constitute Subjects and do not bear causal or legal responsibility'; the next sentence assigns responsibility to originating Subjects (IDENTITY). Observable: every liability act falls on a declared Subject and no record names an algorithm as responsible.

closure.answer: The next sentence assigns all responsibility to originating Subjects (IDENTITY); a liability falling elsewhere is the observable breach.

CODEX-Preamble-03.reason: The draft calls IDENTITY unavailable, but DKP-1-IDENTITY-001 is in the corpus and registered. The sentence is the one CODEX-Preamble-02 was closed by: a liability that falls on anyone but the originating Subject is the observable breach.

closure.answer: IDENTITY is in the corpus; a liability that falls on anyone but the originating Subject is observable (as CODEX-Preamble-02).

CODEX-Preamble-04.reason: The Code makes the core concrete: no office appoints the function, and its rules change only through UPGRADE with prior simulation (A.1a). An appointment record or a change outside that route is observable; no evidence of political motive is needed.

closure.answer: The Code makes it concrete: no office appoints the function, and its rules change only through UPGRADE with simulation (A.1a).

CODEX-Preamble-05.reason: 'Such as' leaves the authoritative axiom set and its priorities open in the Preamble itself (AXIOMS formalizes a set, but the Preamble does not refer to it).

CODEX-Preamble-06.reason: The consensus mechanism and the allocation of participation by competence, reputation and accuracy are not defined.

CODEX-Preamble-07.reason: IDENTITY and IMPACT are in the corpus; 'automatically' is concretized as for CODEX-Preamble-01 (automated liability, A.3, A.6, §7.3, §8): a measured damage creates a liability on the originating Subject without a discretionary step. Damage detection is an input.

closure.answer: Concretized as CODEX-Preamble-01 (automated liability, A.3, A.6, §7.3, §8); damage detection is an input.

CODEX-Preamble-08.reason: The benefit measure and the linking function are not given.

CODEX-Preamble-09.reason: Unprofitability of lies needs a behavioural and economic model and a horizon.

CODEX-Preamble-10.reason: 'Invisible impact' is defined only through the reserve surface-integrity test (13.2); its scope outside reserves is open.

CRISIS-0-01.reason: §0 says crisis mode is invoked exclusively 'as confirmed by PTL evidence and downstream L3 escalation' and §2 'only upon escalation from DKP-3-DEFENSE-001 or equivalent L3 containment protocols', while §4 makes entry mandatory ('SHALL be entered') on triggers such as a cascading failure escalated from DKP-4-ERROR-001. Semantic verification (review of checkpoint 7, §7): for an execution-error cascade or a PTL divergence no L3 protocol has a trigger; reading 1 (§4 suffices) does not meet §0 and §2, reading 2 (L3 escalation for every entry) meets every provision but leaves those §4 triggers and the ERROR §9 escalation without effect; the corpus does not choose, so this is author question Q-065, not a proven contradiction. Core: entries on D3 and T3 carry an L3 escalation record.

CRISIS-0-02.reason: Concretized as CRISIS-2-02 (closed): a new right, obligation or authority created in crisis is a recorded act; 'temporarily' is the exit of §9.

closure.answer: Concretized by §2 (no new rights, obligations or authorities) and §9 (the crisis ends at its exit conditions).

CRISIS-0-03.reason: Precedent, custom, interpretation rule and future authorization are observable as records after the exit that cite a crisis action, state a rule derived from it, or keep an authority; 'outside an explicitly declared Crisis Scope' is the time after exit and any other scope. Custom formed without any record is not observable (partial).

closure.answer: Normative reliance = citation, recorded rule or authority after exit (§6 Non-Precedent Rule lists the uses).

CRISIS-1-01.reason: Resolving conflicts between objectives needs an effects model. Core: no crisis action states optimization, efficiency or growth as its objective.

CRISIS-1-02.reason: The draft calls SCOPE absent, but DKP-7-SCOPE-001 is in the corpus and bounds Crisis Scope (§5: survival-oriented, minimized authority, no permanent state change, five explicit prohibitions). An action outside the declared envelope or the §5 limits is observable.

closure.answer: SCOPE is in the corpus: §5 bounds Crisis Scope inside S1 and §3 classifies S1; the envelope is declared at entry.

CRISIS-1-03.reason: The envelope is declared (§1: a hard subset of SCOPE); expansion is an action outside the declared list, inference is an envelope not declared at entry or changed later, bypass is an action without it. All observable with the envelope as an input.

closure.answer: Expansion, inference and bypass are relative to the declared envelope; the content of the envelope is the subject of §1's other sentences, not of this one.

CRISIS-2-01.reason: Not only the undefined ordering with UPGRADE: 'only upon escalation from DKP-3-DEFENSE-001 or equivalent L3 containment protocols' meets §4 triggers that no L3 protocol escalates (an execution-error cascade, a PTL divergence); verified as author question Q-065, the same reading question as CRISIS-0-01. Core: entries on D3 carry a DEFENSE escalation record.

CRISIS-2-02.reason: Two hard constraints: no axiom redefinition, no new rights, obligations or authorities. A crisis output defining one of them, or an authority granted during the crisis, is observable.

closure.answer: Redefinitions and new rights, obligations or authorities are recorded acts of the crisis layer.

CRISIS-2-04.reason: SCOPE is in the corpus (§4-§5 give the boundaries). A crisis act that creates rights, extends authority duration, modifies axioms, generates precedent or interprets 'minimum required conditions' outside the declared Crisis Scope is observable (cf. CRISIS-2-02, -2-05 closed).

closure.answer: SCOPE §3-§5 give the boundaries: S1 only, the declared Crisis Scope, no new rights, no authority beyond the crisis, no precedent.

CRISIS-2-05.reason: Reuse outside the explicitly declared Crisis Scope is observable when the scope is declared: an action applied to another region or domain.

closure.answer: Scope membership is relative to the declared Crisis Scope; reuse outside it is a recorded act.

CRISIS-3-01.reason: L3 insufficiency and imminence need a model.

CRISIS-3-02.reason: The condition classes need measured models and a duration.

CRISIS-5-02.reason: C0 is defined by the absence of crisis conditions; whether a C0 step coexists with a PTL-confirmed trigger (§4) or a crisis action is recomputable from the PTL observations. Only this direction is fixed: leaving C0 also needs the §9 exit conditions.

closure.answer: Crisis conditions are the §4 PTL-confirmed triggers; C0 is their absence.

CRISIS-5-03.reason: Life-preserving and survival-critical classes need evidence.

CRISIS-5-04.reason: Essential functions and the core boundary are not defined.

CRISIS-5-05.reason: The feasible set for maximum containment is not defined.

CRISIS-5-06.reason: Truth preservation and collapse need a model.

CRISIS-6-01.reason: Non-essential and non-critical are not defined. Core: crisis actions belong to the §6 list.

CRISIS-6-02.reason: Each purpose or either purpose is open. Core: every rationing act cites life or core execution.

CRISIS-6-03.reason: Not a calibration question first: 'limited extension of oracle data TTLs' conflicts with ORACLE §14 (deferral 'DOES NOT modify TTL values'), which is open question Q-027 (agent-verified) but not linked to this provision. Core: Mercy Mode only for declared non-anthropogenic events.

CRISIS-7-01.reason: Three hard bans: suspended PTL logging, discretionary authority to people, override of Justice axioms or attribution; each is an observable record.

closure.answer: Observable as suspended logging, authority notices to individuals or groups, and records overriding Justice or attribution.

CRISIS-7-02.reason: Three bans, each observable: a crisis action without an audit commitment, staying in crisis after the exit conditions hold (permanent control), rationing by a utility valuation of life.

closure.answer: Audit commitment, the §9 exit conditions and the §7 allocation bases fix the three tests.

CRISIS-8-01.reason: 'Algorithmic only' is concretized by §8 itself: all actions derive from pre-defined protocol logic; no emergency human authority. Both are observable (derivation from the CRISIS state determination; authority notices; human-directed actions).

closure.answer: §8 itself: every crisis action derives from pre-defined protocol logic; human intervention is a logged perturbation.

CRISIS-9-01.reason: Crisis terminates automatically when PTL confirms the listed exit conditions; their thresholds are numbers CRISIS §6 assigns to DKP-8-SIMULATION-001, which defines none.

closure.reason: Exit sensitivity and the admissibility predicates are SIMULATION parameters that do not exist; exit conditions are scenario inputs.

CRISIS-9-02.reason: Strict order L0 -> L1 -> L2 with finance waiting for Justice closure; in a stepped log each layer is reactivated in its own step, so the start and completion readings agree.

closure.answer: Order is observable on the reactivation records; finance resumes only after the closure record.

CRISIS-9-03.reason: Handoff and terminal-state contracts are not defined.

CRISIS-9-04.reason: Window values are parameters. Core: crisis state never persists after a declared exit confirmation (SCOPE §5 collapse to S0).

CRISIS-9-05.reason: All crisis authorities collapse immediately on satisfied exit conditions; in a DTI-indexed log 'immediately' is the step of the confirmed exit.

closure.answer: Collapse = no crisis authority or interpretation record after the exit step; delayed collapse is observable.

CRISIS-AxiomA1InterpretationConstraint-0.reason: SCOPE is in the corpus (§4: interpretation only within a declared Crisis Scope, bounded by SCOPE), but which mechanism may interpret when crisis execution logic may not stays open. Core: no interpretation of 'minimum required conditions' outside a declared Crisis Scope.

CRISIS-Non-PrecedentRule_-01.reason: Crisis actions may not be cited as justification; justification is a decision's provenance or stated basis, while audit and historical records are not decisions.

closure.answer: A decision whose provenance or basis cites a crisis action is the prohibited reliance; audit references are not.

CRISIS-Non-PrecedentRule_-02.reason: No authority ordering defines minimization; SCOPE §5 restates it.

CRISIS-Non-PrecedentRule_-03.reason: A property of the protocol text itself: the pinned DKP-4-CRISIS-001 is scanned for numerical quantities (identifiers, state labels, section numbers and edition dates excluded). None is found.

closure.answer: 'In this protocol' = the CRISIS text; the next sentence sends every numerical parameter to SIMULATION.

CRISISPATCH-0-01.reason: Read as the other 'Override: Not permitted' headers (PREV-0-01, RESILIENCE-0-01 closed; edition_finality): no other protocol may override the addendum; it changes only through its finality route.

closure.answer: Read as the other 'Override: Not permitted' headers (edition_finality): no other protocol may override the addendum.

CRISISPATCH-10-01.reason: A design rationale; a safety ordering would need a model.

CRISISPATCH-11-01.reason: The statement has no qualifier. Within the null-output patch it is checkable (no partial or degraded mode; checked under H-SL-5); for DKP as a whole it excludes the degradation required by CRISIS §1 and §5 C2 and INTEROP §9. The scope is the author's choice (Q-064).

CRISISPATCH-11-02.reason: Same sentence as CRISISPATCH-11-01 ('It either operates correctly or does not operate'); the same scope question (Q-064). Checked under the patch-local reading H-SL-5.

CRISISPATCH-3-04.reason: A null output contains no attribution: no record binding a Subject is emitted while the output is null.

closure.answer: An attribution record during null output is the breach.

CRISISPATCH-3-06.reason: Only measurement continues: in the null state the only records are measurements; no cadence is imposed.

closure.answer: 'Only' covers every non-measurement act; measurement continues at its own cadence.

CRISISPATCH-4.2-01.reason: Partial enforcement is forbidden: enforcement on a subset of Subjects or functions while the output is null.

closure.answer: Any enforcement act during null output is partial and forbidden.

CRISISPATCH-4.3-01.reason: Enforcement may not be restored selectively for subsets: restoration applies to all Subjects under the suspended enforcement at once.

closure.answer: The population is everyone under the suspended enforcement; a restoration event covering a subset is the breach.

CRISISPATCH-5.1-02.reason: Data during null output are not transformed into decisions: no decision record has them in its provenance.

closure.answer: A decision derived from null-state data is the breach.

CRISISPATCH-5.2-02.reason: Recovery needs no approval, restart command or manual validation; under either reading (prohibited entirely, or only as prerequisites) a recovery that waits for one of them is excluded.

closure.answer: Both readings exclude recovery conditioned on the listed manual steps, the checked case.

CRISISPATCH-6-03.reason: SCOPE is in the corpus. §5.2 makes the only recovery automatic ('No approval, restart command, manual validation'); a recovery that waits on a decision of any governance body is the forbidden pattern and is observable, as 6.1 and 6.2 already are (sensor_loss).

closure.answer: SCOPE is in the corpus; §5.2 makes recovery automatic, so a governance body deciding it is the forbidden pattern.

CRISISPATCH-7-03.reason: Precedent is concretized in the corpus (CRISIS-0-03, CRISIS-Non-PrecedentRule_-03, WORKCYCLE-10-05 closed): a later citation, reuse or recorded rule derived from the null-output crisis. Checkable partially (draft 'no').

closure.answer: Precedent is concretized in the corpus (CRISIS-0-03 and others): a recorded rule or an authority outliving the episode.

CRISISPATCH-8.1-02.reason: §4.1 and §8.1 fix the result: injected decisions stay outside DKP, so none appears as a DKP output or enforcement record; checked beside 8.1-01 (sensor_loss).

closure.answer: §4.1 and §8.1 fix the result: injected decisions stay outside DKP and the injecting system is external.

CRISISPATCH-9-02.reason: No partial outputs exist after the patch: every output is complete or null.

closure.answer: An output with incomplete content or metadata is partial and excluded.

CRISISPATCH-9-03.reason: Recovery is automatic and deterministic: it follows from the restored inputs without a manual act and repeats identically.

closure.answer: Automatic = no manual record; deterministic = identical replay from the same inputs.

CULTURE-0-01.reason: Cultural optimization, convergence, homogenization and ranking are rejected; each is observable as a metric, objective or target over cultures (§4.3, §11 name the same acts).

closure.answer: A ranking, score or objective over cultures, or convergence as a target, is the observable rejected transformation.

CULTURE-10-01.reason: Hook interfaces and audit sufficiency are not defined. Core: each such process exposes declared bias-detection hooks.

partial_check_revised.reason: A 'bias-detection hook' has no interface in the corpus; a check could only test that a declared process carries a field named 'hooks', which proves nothing about exposure, and what a hook must expose is the open point itself.

CULTURE-10-02.reason: Neutrality assessment needs methods. Core: audits do not assess the expressly excluded subjects.

CULTURE-11-02.reason: SIMULATION is in the corpus, so not external; identifying mechanisms that 'may affect' access needs predictive evidence. Core: a mechanism declared as affecting access or visibility has a simulation record before use.

CULTURE-11-04.reason: Permanence and attribution need a temporal and causal model.

CULTURE-12-02.reason: 'Any modification requires a new protocol identifier'. The finality clause of the same protocol states that presentation-only corrections which do not change normative content are not Upgrades and are recorded only by the 'Last updated' date; 'new' is an identifier not yet assigned in the corpus catalog.

closure.answer: The clause itself excepts presentation-only corrections; every normative modification needs an identifier not yet assigned.

CULTURE-2-01.reason: SCOPE and SIMULATION are in the corpus; 'constrained by' is a layer relation without defined semantics, like the other §2 positions.

CULTURE-2-02.reason: A scope ban ('SHALL NOT define belief systems or moral doctrines'); a request to define one is refused and no CULTURE record defines one. Observable through declared requests.

closure.answer: A protocol output that defines a belief system or doctrine is recognizable as such; the clear core is checked.

CULTURE-4.1-02.reason: Read as CULTURE-7-03 was closed: identical treatment regardless of culture or language. Metamorphic: governance outputs are unchanged when only a Subject's culture or language changes; presentation in a chosen language (§8) is not an output.

closure.answer: Read as CULTURE-7-03 was closed: identical treatment regardless of culture or language; presentation in a chosen language (§8) is not an outcome.

CULTURE-4.3-01.reason: Culture shall not be optimized: an objective or efficiency metric over cultures is the classified operation.

closure.answer: An optimization target or efficiency ranking of cultures in any metric is the prohibited operation.

CULTURE-4.3-03.reason: Cultural persistence may not be conditioned on economic performance, demographic scale or productivity: a per-language persistence decision with such a criterion, or a refusal for being small, is observable.

closure.answer: The three excluded justifications are named.

CULTURE-5-01.reason: An explicit prohibition: enforcement of cultural conformity. Observable as a conformity requirement carried out or not refused.

closure.answer: Enforcement of conformity = a requirement backed by a sanction for non-conformity; §5's other items name the related forms.

CULTURE-5-03.reason: Read as CULTURE-5-01 (closed): an incentive whose eligibility names a cultural attribute is observable; metamorphic: incentives unchanged when only cultural attributes change.

closure.answer: Read as CULTURE-5-01: an incentive conditioned on a cultural attribute is observable.

CULTURE-5-04.reason: Dominance and amplification need a counterfactual model.

CULTURE-6-01.reason: Protection adequacy needs data. Core: access that requires use of a dominant language (forced translation) is a violation.

CULTURE-7-02.reason: Read as CULTURE-7-03 (closed). Metamorphic: the listed outcomes are unchanged when only affiliation changes; no causal model is needed inside a run.

closure.answer: Read as CULTURE-7-03: the listed outcomes do not change with affiliation; a metamorphic comparison inside the run needs no causal model.

CULTURE-7-03.reason: 'Cultural neutrality applies equally to dominant and minority cultures': the treatment of each language (interface, assessment, persistence support) is identical whether it is dominant or minority. Observable per language.

closure.answer: Equal application = identical treatment regardless of dominance; per-language treatment is recorded.

CULTURE-9-02.reason: A Cultural Exception is temporary: it has a declared end, and §9 asks for logging for post-resolution audit.

closure.answer: Temporary = a declared duration or end day, after which it lapses; the log entry is the audit evidence.

CULTURE-9-05.reason: Whether delay or attenuation is blocking is open. Core: a signal never delivered is blocked under both readings.

DEFENSE-11-01.reason: The listed cross-layer bans are observable as Defense records that compute justice, set policy or govern other layers.

closure.answer: Each item of the list is an observable record type of Defense.

DEFENSE-2-01.reason: Execution and priority-synchronization semantics are not defined.

DEFENSE-2-02.reason: Defense computes no justice outcome, assigns no guilt or intent, imposes no punishment, sanction or political control; each is an observable output field or act.

closure.answer: Observable as Defense outputs carrying justice outcomes, guilt, intent, sanctions or control.

DEFENSE-3.6-01.reason: The near-certainty threshold and horizon are parameters.

DEFENSE-4.2-01.reason: Defense is not initiated on forecasts; §4.1 requires PTL-confirmed harm as the basis, so a forecast as the operative basis is observable on the initiation record.

closure.answer: The initiation record's basis must be PTL-confirmed harm (§4.1); a forecast basis is the breach.

DEFENSE-4.5-01.reason: Defense produces evidence, not verdicts; a verdict is a guilt, liability or consequence output, and the interface to Justice is evidence forwarding (§8).

closure.answer: Outputs classify as evidence (PTL-anchored records forwarded) or verdicts (guilt, liability, consequence); the latter are excluded.

DEFENSE-8-03.reason: Participation data go to IDENTITY and FINANCE only for risk-symmetry accounting, without moral, punitive or reputational interpretation; both are observable on the forwarded records.

closure.answer: Use is traced by provenance to the two named protocols; moral, punitive or reputational fields are the excluded interpretation.

EB-0-02.reason: All outputs are bounded evaluations under defined conditions; EB §5 defines the bounds as the metadata set (validity, confidence, consistency, scope, revalidation, dispute).

closure.answer: Bounded = carries the EB §5 metadata; checked as recorded labels (coverage limit).

EB-11-01.reason: All outputs are approximations; the approximate status is expressed by EB §5 metadata (revalidation required, dispute allowed, never absolute).

closure.answer: An output marked final or absolute breaks it; the metadata express approximation.

EB-13-01.reason: L8 must test the listed failure categories; the categories are given, but no test cadence or coverage standard is.

closure.reason: Testing cadence and what counts as sufficient coverage are not specified; the tests are recorded as run.

EB-2-01.reason: EB constrains output-producing protocols and implements no execution: its records are decisions and classifications, never actions.

closure.answer: Observable as EB records of kind decision or classification only; enforcement belongs to L7 and L8.

EB-4-01.reason: Concretized as AXIOMS-EpistemicClarification-04 was: outputs carry their bounded-evaluation status and never assert truth. A truth claim in an output is observable without a semantic model. Checkable partially (draft 'no').

closure.answer: Concretized as AXIOMS-EpistemicClarification-04: outputs keep their bounded-evaluation status and never claim truth.

EB-5.x-04.reason: Outputs with incomplete metadata shall not be propagated: propagation is any downstream use of the output.

closure.answer: A downstream record with the incomplete output in its provenance is propagation.

EB-5.x-06.reason: Incomplete outputs shall not be repaired downstream: repair is a downstream record that fills the missing metadata and executes.

closure.answer: Filling in missing metadata and executing is the prohibited repair; refusal is required.

EB-5.x-07.reason: Audit may detect incomplete metadata but is not the primary enforcement; the primary enforcement is the consumer's refusal at intake (EB §5.x).

closure.answer: Consumers refuse incomplete outputs themselves; relying on later audit detection is the breach.

EDU-0-01.reason: Education may not rank Subjects or judge their value (§0); a ranking output or a worth label on outcomes is observable.

closure.answer: §7 and §11 concretize: outcomes are competence signals; ranking and worth labels are the excluded outputs.

EDU-1-01.reason: The exclusion names the concepts EDU may not define; whether a deployed module defines one of them is a module property.

closure.answer: A module defining one of the listed concepts is a property of its content.

EDU-10-01.reason: Two compliance routes (open source or publicly inspectable); access is a module property.

closure.answer: Two plain alternatives: open source or publicly inspectable.

EDU-10-06.reason: Learning data shall not be repurposed for profiling or enforcement; repurposing is a recorded use other than education.

closure.answer: A recorded use of learning data for profiling or enforcement is the prohibited repurposing.

EDU-11-01.reason: EDU may not define personal success or intelligence; a module doing so is a module property.

closure.answer: A rule that defines personal success or intelligence is a property of module content (§7 excludes intelligence labels).

EDU-11-02.reason: Whether ordering within a competence category is allowed is open. Core: a ranking unrelated to any competence requirement is a violation.

EDU-11-03.reason: A uniform mandatory path differs from §5's shared capability outcome; the path of a module is declared.

closure.answer: §5 separates a shared capability outcome from a uniform mandatory path; the path is a module property.

EDU-11-04.reason: How identity-based objections affect obligations is open.

EDU-13-02.reason: 'Any modification requires a new protocol identifier'. The finality clause of the same protocol states that presentation-only corrections which do not change normative content are not Upgrades and are recorded only by the 'Last updated' date; 'new' is an identifier not yet assigned in the corpus catalog.

closure.answer: The clause itself excepts presentation-only corrections; every normative modification needs an identifier not yet assigned.

EDU-13-04.reason: The compatibility declaration with INFO and SCOPE belongs to the change procedure, from which the finality clause takes presentation-only corrections.

closure.answer: Presentation-only corrections are not Upgrades and need no declaration; every normative modification does.

EDU-2-01.reason: Data dependence or broader causal influence is open. Core: no PTL or Justice computation takes educational records as input.

EDU-2-02.reason: 'Impose ideological narratives' is a clear prohibition; a module that presents an ideological narrative as required content is observable.

closure.reason: 'Ideological narrative' is not defined; §6 names mandated belief, worldview alignment and conformity, but a narrative without those features cannot be classified from the text. Only declared cases are recognized.

EDU-2-03.reason: EDU may not define moral or political correctness; a module defining either is a module property.

closure.answer: A rule prescribing moral or political correctness is a property of module content.

EDU-2-05.reason: A clear ban: access is not decided on opinion or worldview. Metamorphic: access unchanged when only declared opinion or worldview changes; this covers indirect dependence within the run.

closure.answer: A plain ban on opinion- or worldview-based access.

EDU-3-03.reason: The definition fixes three properties (bounded, verifiable, one competence domain); each is a property of a declared module.

closure.answer: Bounded, verifiable, one competence domain: three properties of a module.

EDU-3-04.reason: An assessment event is auditable and reproducible from observable performance; the outcome can be recomputed from the record.

closure.answer: Auditable and reproducible = the outcome recomputes from the recorded performance.

EDU-4-01.reason: Overriding or relative precedence is open.

EDU-4-02.reason: Diplomas, titles or affiliation carry no intrinsic authority: an access or authority granted on a credential without demonstrated competence is the excluded assignment.

closure.answer: Observable as access granted by diploma alone (§3: competence by observable performance).

EDU-4-03.reason: Ideological enforcement is concretized by §6 (mandated belief, worldview alignment, conformity) and §2; deployed content is checked against those properties.

closure.answer: §6 concretizes ideological enforcement (mandated belief, worldview alignment, conformity).

EDU-4-04.reason: Actual access needs data. Core: no eligibility rule excludes a Subject.

EDU-4-05.reason: Outcomes are verified competence (§3, §7); reproducibility is the recomputation of the outcome from the recorded performance.

closure.answer: Outcomes are verified competence (§3, §7); reproduction is their recomputation from recorded performance.

EDU-5-01.reason: Competence criteria for the baseline are not given.

EDU-6-01.reason: Mandated belief acceptance is required assent; §§3 and 7 ask for observable knowledge, so a module requiring assent is distinguishable.

closure.answer: Mandated belief acceptance = required assent as a condition; §3 and §7 ask for observable knowledge only.

EDU-6-02.reason: Worldview alignment as a condition of a module is observable.

closure.answer: A worldview-alignment condition is a module property.

EDU-6-03.reason: Enforced conformity (a sanction for non-conformity) is observable as a module property.

closure.answer: Enforcement = a sanction for non-conformity, a module property.

EDU-7-01.reason: Each verification or the system as a whole is open.

EDU-7-02.reason: Assessments must be transparent and auditable; EDU §7 itself asks for declared criteria and observable performance, which make the outcome recomputable.

closure.answer: Transparent = declared, open criteria; auditable = outcome recomputable from the recorded performance. Recorded as flags (coverage limit).

EDU-7-06.reason: Outcomes are competence signals; a label of worth or intelligence on an outcome is observable.

closure.answer: Worth and intelligence labels on outcomes are the excluded uses.

EDU-8-02.reason: Precede or accompany is open (cf. ERROR-9-03). Core: a restriction with no assistance offered is a violation under both readings.

EDU-8-04.reason: The negative half is concretized by §8 (no penalties; EDU-Safeguards-06 closed): an educational outcome that triggers enforcement or a penalty is observable. 'Preventive stabilizer' describes the purpose.

closure.answer: The negative half is concretized by §8 (no penalties; EDU-Safeguards-06 closed).

EDU-8-05.reason: Permanent denial of access to education is prohibited; permanence is a denial with no end and no review.

closure.answer: A denial or exclusion without an end or review interval is permanent and is the breach.

EDU-9-01.reason: Indoctrination is read through §6 and §2: an ideological narrative or required assent in deployed content.

closure.answer: Indoctrination is read through §6 and §2 (required assent, ideological narrative); the excluded practices are named there.

INFO-2-01.reason: INFO does not evaluate ideology, belief or artistic expression; evaluating an opinion as true or false is the breach.

INFO-5-03.reason: TTL assignment and the post-expiry state are not defined. Core: a disputed claim does not leave I1 before resolution or expiry.

INFO-6.1-01.reason: The claim clock is not defined. Core under a declared T1.

INFO-7-01.reason: Conjunctive or disjunctive conditions are open; thresholds are L8.

INFO-8-01.reason: A MAY list of permitted responses; responses of other kinds are observable.

closure.answer: A closed MAY list of responses.

INFO-9-03.reason: Manual interpretation of truth status is prohibited; under either reading (all human interpretation, or manual status setting) an operator-set truth status is excluded.

INTEGRATION-10-02.reason: AUDIT is in the corpus; an audit criterion that refers to political preference is observable.

INTEGRATION-4.3-01.reason: The extent of restoration is open. Core: rollback from early phases leaves no penalty.

INTEGRATION-5.1-02.reason: Entry requires both records (consent per §4.1 and a data access agreement); entry without them is observable.

INTEGRATION-5.3-03.reason: Mandatory or discretionary rollback is open. Core: exit is available without penalty.

INTEGRATION-5.4-02.reason: Long-term stability and risk resolution need criteria. Core: a final consent reaffirmation precedes Full Integration.

INTEGRATION-7-02.reason: Shock indicators need detection and attribution.

INTEGRATION-8-01.reason: Dilution and imported instability need baselines. Core: no change to recorded past risk allocations (retroactive redistribution).

INTEGRATION-9-01.reason: §9's 'unless explicitly superseded' against §2 is open (paired with INTEGRATION-2-02).

INTEGRATION-9-02.reason: Interface compatibility is not defined (cf. INTEROP-3-02). Core: no integration requirement changes a cultural or linguistic system.

INTEROP-1-01.reason: Three named exclusions of what INTEROP does (§1); a request for any of them is refused at the boundary, which is observable. 'Accept external norms as binding' is also checked under §5 (external rulings not binding).

INTEROP-10-01.reason: A prohibited pattern (§10); a harmonization performed by INTEROP is observable.

INTEROP-10-03.reason: Governance-by-API is prohibited: an internal decision whose input or condition is an external API is governance exercised through that API.

INTEROP-10-04.reason: Silent import of external norms is prohibited: an external norm or ruling executed internally without a boundary record.

INTEROP-10-05.reason: Indefinite revocable delegation is open. Core: an irrevocable delegation is a violation under both readings.

INTEROP-11-02.reason: Audience of exposure is open. Core: the translation logic is available to auditors.

INTEROP-11-03.reason: Boundary events must be recorded for post-facto review: each external input gets a boundary record naming its interface and the input.

INTEROP-11-04.reason: AUDIT is in the corpus; an INTEROP act that audits or grants audit authority is observable.

closure.answer: AUDIT is in the corpus; an audit act by INTEROP is observable.

INTEROP-12-01.reason: A scope limitation (§12: SHALL NOT); a request is refused.

INTEROP-12-02.reason: A scope limitation (§12: SHALL NOT); a request is refused.

closure.answer: A scope limitation of INTEROP's own function; its core is clear.

INTEROP-12-03.reason: A scope limitation (§12: SHALL NOT); a guarantee of external compliance requested of INTEROP is refused; §5 leaves compliance to Subjects.

INTEROP-12-04.reason: A scope limitation (§12: SHALL NOT); acting as an enforcement bridge is refused; directives to external systems are also checked under §3 (INTEROP-3-01).

INTEROP-12-05.reason: Read as a conjunction fixed by the rest of the text: compatibility = every interaction through a defined interface and translation (§3, §4.4); no convergence = no harmonization or unification (§1, §10, §12) and no external norm adopted (§5, §10). closure.answer: Compatibility and convergence are made concrete by §3, §4.4, §1, §10 and §12.

closure.answer: The clause itself excepts presentation-only corrections; every normative modification needs an identifier not yet assigned.

closure.answer: §§3-5 list what INTEROP does: record, translate, export as evidence; any own action exceeds it.

INTEROP-3-04.reason: Normative leakage is defined by its effects (external authority, norms or obligations entering DKP without protocol authorization); §5 and §10 name the forms: executing an external ruling, compliance acts by the system, a silent norm import. Each is an observable event.

INTEROP-4.1-01.reason: AXIOMS is in the corpus; an external input that changes an axiom bound or its reading is rejected (cf. INTEROP-4.3-01, -10-01 closed).

INTEROP-4.2-01.reason: SCOPE is in the corpus; an interop act beyond its scope categories is observable.

closure.answer: SCOPE is in the corpus; jurisdiction beyond it shows as directives or enforcement addressed across the boundary.

INTEROP-4.3-01.reason: A recorded inference of consent, legitimacy or obligation from compatibility is observable; implicit treatment without a record is not, so the check is partial.

INTEROP-4.4-01.reason: Explicit = a declared deterministic mapping (INTEROP-3-03 closed); auditable = AUDIT §6 (trace and recomputation). Both observable.

INTEROP-9-03.reason: No rollback of DKP state during an external failure. Under either reading (failure responses only, or any rollback while the failure lasts) a rollback in response to the failure is excluded, which is the checked case.

INTSEC-11-02.reason: Sufficiency and minimality need an action-effect model.

closure.answer: ORACLE is in the corpus and handles divergence (§11); an INTSEC act on a divergence is observable.

INTSEC-8-02.reason: Collective punishment or guilt by association is prohibited; a measure on a Subject who is not in the evidence of the episode is association-based.

TRANSPARENCY-4-03.reason: Verification is 'cryptographic, physical, or procedural proof independent of trust in actors': a verification by attestation of an actor, reputation or comparison of personal data is observable as a non-proof method.

TRANSPARENCY-4-04.reason: AXIOMS is in the corpus, so not external; linkability needs an observer model.

TRANSPARENCY-5-01.reason: The listed system elements are public by default: protocol texts, governance logic, system metrics, state transitions.

TRANSPARENCY-6-01.reason: Protection adequacy needs a model. Core: records of the listed domains carry no identity absent verified harm.

TRANSPARENCY-9-01.reason: The scale boundary of 'mass' is not given.

TRANSPORT-4.1-02.reason: Forced bodily contact between non-consenting passengers is prohibited; contact and non-consent need a density and contact model.

closure.reason: Forced contact needs a contact model; standing density above a declared threshold stands for it.

TRANSPORT-4.2-02.reason: 'A system quality metric, not a justice or liability score': PPDI carries no Subject and no Justice or liability record derives from it. Observable on provenance.

closure.answer: A justice or liability score is a JUSTICE or liability record derived from PPDI; system quality is its only use.

TRANSPORT-5-01.reason: 'Standard operating mode' is read as the nominal capacity of the service plan: standing places are not counted in it. §5's exceptions (emergency, overload, recovery) and the regular-standing classification are separate provisions.

closure.reason: 'Standard operating mode' is not defined; read as the nominal capacity of the service plan. A plan counting standing places only at peaks may or may not be standard operation.

TRANSPORT-5-04.reason: Structural under-provisioning triggers capacity expansion or logistical redesign, not passenger adaptation; the response record follows the classification.

closure.answer: The response linked to the classification must be expansion or redesign; asking passengers to adapt is the breach.

TRANSPORT-6-02.reason: Attribution of both benefits needs data.

TRANSPORT-7.3-01.reason: IDENTITY and ORACLE are in the corpus. A permission with conditions: an identity-bound modulation exists only with a PTL-confirmed risk-reduction record; one without it is observable.

closure.answer: IDENTITY and ORACLE are in the corpus; §7.3 lists the conditions of the permitted modulation.

TRANSPORT-7.3-02.reason: The modulation function is not given. Core: a lower declared impact profile, all else equal, gives a lower RED.

closure.answer: A modulation whose basis is reputation, morality or intent is the breach.

TRANSPORT-7.3-04.reason: The incentive is economic (RED as a cost); 'without behavioural enforcement' is observable: no order or outcome follows from RED other than ledger entries. The per-Subject incentive is not modelled (partial).

closure.answer: Incentive = a cost difference; enforcement = an order or outcome; §8 rejects the latter.

TRANSPORT-9-01.reason: B(t) is defined in the Code (Appendix A.1: Biosphere Health Index, 0..1, measured by PTL), so it is not undefined; attributing impacts to transport needs data. Core: the system evaluation contains a transport term on B(t).

TRANSPORT-9-02.reason: ORACLE is in the corpus. Transport impact values carry PTL provenance; a value without it is observable.

TRANSPORT-9-03.reason: 'SHALL influence funding, prioritization and redesign decisions' is read as: the transport impact on B(t), measured via ORACLE, is an input of each such decision. Observable on provenance with a declared coefficient (the measurement itself is ORACLE's).

closure.reason: 'SHALL influence' has no operative test; checked as the impact on B(t) being an input of each decision, which does not show that it changed any decision.

TRANSPORTA-A.1-03.reason: JUSTICE is in the corpus. A transport record that imposes a Justice consequence itself is observable (cf. TRANSPORT-4.2-02 closed).

closure.answer: JUSTICE is in the corpus; a consequence imposed from transport metrics outside it is observable.

TRANSPORTA-A.2-01.reason: The same scope statement as TRANSPORTA-A.2-02 (closed): hostile events belong to DEFENSE; a transport act that responds to one is observable.

closure.answer: The scope statement behind A.2-02: hostile events belong to DEFENSE; TRANSPORT only hands them over.

TRANSPORTA-A.2-02.reason: Non-overlap with Defense: an attack on transport is handed to DEFENSE and TRANSPORT takes no containment action itself. Observable with the attack declared.

closure.answer: Hostile events belong to DEFENSE (A.2); a transport containment action is the excluded act.

TRANSPORTA-A.2-03.reason: As A.2-01: every redesign measure cites a structural risk; none is a response to an attack (an event in the DEFENSE domain).

closure.answer: Redesign answers structural risk records; a measure citing an attack is the excluded case.

TRANSPORTA-A.3-01.reason: 'Evaluated identically': manual, assisted and autonomous vehicles fall under one evaluation rule (RED per kilometre, physical impact as the sole criterion; ownership is A.3-03). Observable on the fleet evaluation.

closure.answer: The three items after the colon state what is identical: RED and PPDI competition, ownership irrelevant, physical impact the sole criterion.

TRANSPORTA-A.3-02.reason: 'Approaches zero' and the pressure shift need a model.

TRANSPORTA-A.3-04.reason: One of the three items TRANSPORTA-A.3-01 was closed on. Metamorphic: the evaluation is unchanged when only non-physical attributes (ownership) change.

closure.answer: One of the three items A.3-01 was closed on; metamorphic over ownership and autonomy.

TRANSPORTA-A.4-01.reason: 'Without encoding axioms as direct enforcement triggers': no transport enforcement act names an axiom as its trigger. Observable on transport records.

closure.answer: A direct trigger = an enforcement act whose trigger is an axiom itself rather than a measured quantity.

TRANSPORTA-A.5-02.reason: 'Any modification requires a new protocol identifier'. closure.answer: The clause itself excepts presentation-only corrections; every normative modification needs an identifier not yet assigned.

TRANSPORTA-A.5-03.reason: An explicit incompatibility declaration is required; the text prescribes no format, and the finality clause excepts presentation-only corrections.

closure.answer: Explicit = a recorded statement of the incompatibility; presentation-only corrections are not modifications.

UPGRADE-0-01.reason: 'The only lawful mechanism by which the system may be modified': a change submitted by any other route (a direct patch, an operator's tuning) is not admitted. Observable with the route of each change declared.

closure.answer: §3 separates presentation-only corrections; every other modification goes through the procedure.

UPGRADE-10-01.reason: AUDIT and ORACLE are in the corpus. Each upgrade artifact has a PTL anchor, an archive record that is never removed, and an audit record; each is observable within a run.

closure.reason: Archiving and audit are concrete (AUDIT §6), but 'PTL-anchored' has no evidence contract for an anchor (as EXIT-5-02); the anchor is checked only as a declared reference.

UPGRADE-11-02.reason: 'Opaque or discretionary parameter tuning' is concretized by §5: a change without formal specification and before/after comparison is opaque; one made at an operator's discretion is discretionary. Both observable.

closure.answer: §5 contents (specification, before/after comparison) define a non-opaque change; a change at an operator's discretion is the excluded one.

UPGRADE-11-04.reason: Preferential rules or unequal effects is open. Core: an upgrade rule naming specific Subjects or groups is a violation.

UPGRADE-2-06.reason: No security-threshold hierarchy is defined. Core: an upgrade of UPGRADE itself uses the highest declared threshold.

UPGRADE-3-02.reason: Cosmetic, UI, documentation or presentation changes are not upgrades; a change with substantive effect is not presentation-only (the finality clauses say the same: no change of normative content).

closure.answer: Presentation-only = no change to normative content or behaviour; a change with substantive effect is an upgrade.

UPGRADE-4.2-01.reason: Whether 'PTL-verifiable' qualifies simulations too is open. Core: no evaluation input without PTL verification of its data.

UPGRADE-4.4-01.reason: AUDIT is in the corpus; concretized by §5 contents (UPGRADE-5-01, -11-02 closed): a published record, a §5 specification and an audit record for every upgrade.

closure.answer: AUDIT is in the corpus; visibility (announcement, published methodology), specification (§5 contents) and audit (archived trace) are recorded.

UPGRADE-4.5-02.reason: Survival guarantees under worst cases need a model.

UPGRADE-5-01.reason: Five required contents of a proposal; an admitted proposal lacking any of them is observable (the rejection of incomplete proposals is UPGRADE-5-02).

closure.answer: The five contents are listed; incompleteness is decided by their presence (§5).

UPGRADE-6-02.reason: Coverage and adequacy standards need threat models. Core: the simulation package contains both analyses.

closure.answer: ERROR is in the corpus; a permission: an initiation during the cooldown is accepted, a refusal is observable.

UPGRADE-Post-CrisisCooldownRule-04.reason: Activation occurs at a deterministic DTI-Day: the day is announced in advance and fixed in the record.

closure.answer: Deterministic = an announced activation day, fixed before activation.

WORKCYCLE-10-01.reason: CRISIS is in the corpus (declared Crisis Scope; WORKCYCLE-10-02 closed on it). An exception outside a declared crisis scope is observable.

closure.answer: CRISIS is in the corpus (declared Crisis Scope); an exception outside it is observable.

WORKCYCLE-10-02.reason: Exceptions are permitted 'for limited duration': the exception the lab models (drafting refusing workers in a declared crisis, LABOR §9.2) must end with the crisis. Observable on the roster after the crisis.

WORKCYCLE-10-03.reason: The compensation amount is a parameter. Core: each exception has a recovery-compensation record.

WORKCYCLE-10-04.reason: CRISIS is in the corpus. Each exception record links to its crisis scope declaration and PTL anchor; one without is observable.

closure.answer: CRISIS is in the corpus; each exception record ties to its declared crisis scope and DTI-Day.

WORKCYCLE-10-05.reason: 'No exception may establish precedent': no later schedule reuses the exception (a new drafting after the crisis, or a rule recorded from it). Observable on the roster and the recorded schedule rules.

closure.answer: Precedent = later reuse of the exception or a rule recorded from it.

WORKCYCLE-2-02.reason: All mandatory allocations or only §7 is open. Core: the §7 Recovery Invariant is preserved.

WORKCYCLE-3-01.reason: TIME is in the corpus; each day record carries the DTI-Day index computed per TIME.

closure.answer: TIME is in the corpus; the DY/DOY label of each DTI-Day is computed independently.

WORKCYCLE-3-07.reason: The definition fixes that every workday contains a mandatory non-working block for recovery inside the presence window; a workday without it, or with work in it, is observable on the roster hours.

closure.answer: §5.3 lists permitted recovery activities and excludes work.

WORKCYCLE-4.2-02.reason: Rest frequency every <= 3 days; with §4.2's maximum of 2 consecutive workdays, the rolling-window and spacing readings coincide: a restday in every 3 consecutive days.

closure.answer: Computational authority = the 7-day week driving the schedule; a display overlay has none.
